question: What is the main goal of a Drug Revolving Fund (DRF) in a clinic or hospital?

options.A: To generate huge profits for hospital management
options.B: To store expired medications safely before disposal
options.C: To maintain a continuous and steady supply of essential drugs
options.D: To provide free medical treatment to all citizens

explanation: You've got this! The whole point of a DRF is to make sure essential medicines never run out. Money collected from sales is used right away to buy fresh stock. Simple and effective!

question: How does keeping a food diary differ from doing a 24-hour dietary recall?

options.A: Food diaries measure blood levels instead of food intake
options.B: Food diaries rely entirely on long-term memory
options.C: Food diaries are only performed by specialized surgeons
options.D: Food diaries record items in real-time as they are consumed

explanation: Writing things down as you eat beats trying to remember everything at the end of the day!

question: Which part of wearing Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) is most risky for accidentally contaminating yourself?

options.A: Donning (putting on) the clean gear
options.B: Storing unused aprons
options.C: Doffing (removing) the contaminated gear
options.D: Walking through the hallway

explanation: Correct! Taking off dirty gear takes the most care because you might accidentally touch germs on the outside. Always follow the steps carefully!

question: What should you do right away if you evaluate your patient and see they haven't met their care goal?

options.A: Wait until the next morning doctor's rounds to report it
options.B: Discontinue all monitoring devices to reduce patient stress
options.C: Reassess the patient and modify the plan of care
options.D: Document that the patient is impossible to treat

explanation: Don't panic if a goal isn't met—that's totally normal nursing! It just means it's time to cycle back, figure out what's going on, and tweak your game plan.

question: A patient gets widespread hives, mild wheezing, and belly cramps 10 minutes after an antibiotic. What kind of reaction is this?

options.A: Moderate
options.B: Delayed
options.C: Severe
options.D: Mild

explanation: When symptoms affect more than one body part—like both the skin and the tummy—we classify it as moderate.

question: Why is it important for a nurse to recognize the physical and psychological signs of early or forced marriage?

options.A: To report the patient to international news agencies for public awareness
options.B: To prescribe financial aid directly from the hospital pharmacy fund
options.C: To automatically discharge the patient without further medical evaluation
options.D: To provide targeted clinical care, appropriate counseling, and safe referrals

explanation: Great job! Recognizing these signs helps nurses deliver specialized medical care, emotional support, and safe links to protective social services.

question: What is a major structural difference between sympathetic and parasympathetic pathways?

options.A: Sympathetic fibers never use ganglia to pass signals along.
options.B: Sympathetic preganglionic fibers are always much longer than postganglionic fibers.
options.C: Parasympathetic nerves only exit through the lumbar spinal cord.
options.D: Parasympathetic ganglia are usually located close to or inside the target organs.

explanation: Because parasympathetic fibers travel a long way from the brain or lower spine before reaching their destination, their relay stations (ganglia) sit right near or inside the target organ walls.

question: Which sign tells you a newborn baby is working too hard to breathe and has respiratory distress?

options.A: Sternal retractions
options.B: Acrocyanosis of hands
options.C: Coupled heart sounds
options.D: Active limb movement

explanation: When the skin pulls in around the chest bones (sternal retractions), it means the baby is struggling to pull air into their lungs. That's a classic warning sign!

question: Why is teaching patients to spot early warning signs of their chronic disease so important?

options.A: It completely cures chronic conditions like diabetes.
options.B: It ensures family members take over all nursing duties.
options.C: It stops patients from ever taking prescription drugs.
options.D: It allows for early action before emergency hospitalization is needed.

explanation: When patients recognize small changes early, they can call for help or adjust care before a scary health crisis lands them in the hospital.

question: Where does an established DRF get most of its ongoing income?

options.A: Fines collected from healthcare workers who arrive late
options.B: Annual gifts from international sports organizations
options.C: Direct monthly donations from private manufacturing companies
options.D: Out-of-pocket user payments from patients buying drugs

explanation: Correct! Every time patients pay for their prescriptions, that money goes right back into keeping the fund alive and well.

question: Two clinical instructors use the exact same rubric to grade your wound dressing, but their scores are wildly different. What does this point to?

options.A: Construct validity
options.B: Content bias
options.C: Formative timing
options.D: Inter-rater reliability

explanation: When different teachers get different scores using the exact same tool on the same student, the tool has an issue with inter-rater reliability. You are mastering the nursing jargon!

question: What does the term 'hidden hunger' mean in public health?

options.A: Micronutrient deficiencies from diets lacking essential vitamins and minerals
options.B: Eating too many high-protein foods in a single meal
options.C: Extreme starvation caused by total crop failure
options.D: A condition where people hide their food out of fear of theft

explanation: Exactly right! Hidden hunger happens when someone gets enough belly-filling calories from cheap starchy foods, but misses out on vital vitamins and minerals.

question: What is the primary focus of pediatric palliative and hospice care at home?

options.A: Finding a cure for chronic genetic disorders
options.B: Enrolling the child in competitive school sports
options.C: Transferring the child back to the intensive care unit
options.D: Maximizing comfort, pain management, and family support

explanation: Well done! Palliative care is all about quality of life, easing pain, and bringing comfort to both the child and their loved ones. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T11#GNS324_U3_T11_h8)

question: How do grassroots community programs directly help HIV orphans?

options.A: They provide localized support like food, school fees, and health checks
options.B: They construct massive industrial factories for child employment
options.C: They enforce mandatory DNA testing for all community members
options.D: They relocate every orphan outside of Nigeria to foreign countries

explanation: Grassroots programs bring practical, everyday assistance directly to the vulnerable children and families who need it most. You are doing brilliantly!

question: Which vitamin is given urgently to prevent permanent brain damage in patients with severe alcoholism?

options.A: Vitamin C
options.B: Riboflavin
options.C: Thiamine
options.D: Vitamin K

explanation: Thiamine (Vitamin B1) is a lifesaver here! Chronic alcohol use can severely deplete it, leading to serious brain issues like Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome. Quick replacement is key.

question: Who is primarily responsible for creating strategic objectives in a hospital?

options.A: Newly hired graduate nurses during orientation
options.B: Patients filling out feedback forms at discharge
options.C: Executive leadership and the board of directors
options.D: External auditors hired to check financial records

explanation: Top executives set long-term strategic targets because they control the organization's overall direction and resources. [learn more](GST321_U2_T3#GST321_U2_T3_h3)

question: What type of waste belongs inside a puncture-resistant safety box?

options.A: Expired food scraps
options.B: Contaminated paperwork
options.C: Empty water bottles
options.D: Sharps and needles

explanation: Safety boxes are specially designed to safely contain sharp objects like needles and blades without letting them pierce through. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T5#GNS122_U5_T5_h2)

question: A nurse manager has limited funds for a ward. Which item should be bought first to keep patients safe?

options.A: Essential life-saving medications and functional oxygen supplies
options.B: Upgraded entertainment systems for the staff break room
options.C: Foreign travel allowances for senior administrative staff members
options.D: Expensive decorative furniture for the manager's private office

explanation: Patient care always comes first! When funds are tight, life-saving drugs and oxygen take priority over office luxuries every single time.

question: What is a key requirement for successful community health education?

options.A: Using complex medical terminology to ensure scientific accuracy
options.B: Adapting the teaching to the cultural context and literacy levels of the audience
options.C: Relying exclusively on written pamphlets without verbal explanations
options.D: Conducting all teaching sessions inside high-tech hospital seminar rooms

explanation: Teaching only works when your audience truly understands it. Always speak in a way that connects with their daily lives and culture!

question: How can a Guinea worm infection lead to permanent joint stiffness?

options.A: Systemic fever dissolves the synovial fluid protecting the joint
options.B: Severe local inflammation near a joint causes scar tissue and contractures
options.C: Patients refuse to move their limbs for the rest of their lives
options.D: The worm directly consumes cartilage and bone marrow inside the joint

explanation: Spot on! Bad inflammation and infection near joints can leave behind tight scar tissue that makes movement difficult. You're thinking deeply about patient outcomes!

question: Which facilities typically represent the tertiary level of health care in Nigeria?

options.A: Primary health care dispensaries in rural villages
options.B: Local government maternity and immunization posts
options.C: Private neighborhood patent medicine shops
options.D: Teaching hospitals and specialist medical centers

explanation: Teaching hospitals and specialized federal medical centers provide the highest level of complex tertiary care. [learn more](GST322_U5_T2#GST322_U5_T2_h4)

question: What is a major environmental factor that increases mosquito breeding and malaria transmission?

options.A: High altitude mountain air with low oxygen levels
options.B: Dense forest canopies blocking all sunlight
options.C: Cool, dry winds blowing during the harmattan season
options.D: Stagnant pools of water after heavy rainfall

explanation: Female mosquitoes lay their eggs in standing water, making puddles and poorly drained areas primary breeding sites after rain. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T14#GNS313_U1_T14_h4)

question: What is the term for white blood cells squeezing through tiny blood vessel walls into injured tissue?

options.A: Vasoconstriction
options.B: Hemostasis
options.C: Apoptosis
options.D: Diapedesis

explanation: Great job! Diapedesis is just the clever way white blood cells slip out of the bloodstream to join the fight at the tissue level.

question: What are the three core action steps of Psychological First Aid?

options.A: Diagnose, Treat, Refer
options.B: Analyze, Process, Cure
options.C: Look, Listen, Link
options.D: Sedate, Calm, Rest

explanation: The three basic action principles of PFA guide helpers to observe safety, listen to needs, and connect people to resources. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T6#GNS315_U5_T6_h6)

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do before using a bed accessory on a patient?

options.A: Apply a thick layer of petroleum jelly to the surface
options.B: Label it with the patient's full home address
options.C: Submerge the entire device in boiling water
options.D: Inspect it for cracks, sharp edges, or loose parts

explanation: Safety first! Always check equipment for any cracks or sharp spots before use to protect your patient from accidental injuries.

question: What is the main job of the sympathetic nervous system?

options.A: Controlling voluntary skeletal muscle movements
options.B: Promoting digestion and nutrient absorption at rest
options.C: Regulating the body's internal temperature during sleep
options.D: Preparing the body for stressful or emergency situations

explanation: Think of the sympathetic system as your body's 'fight-or-flight' alarm. It gets you ready to act fast when danger or heavy stress shows up. You've got this!

question: Which IV solution is classified as isotonic and commonly used for fluid resuscitation?

options.A: 0.9% Normal Saline
options.B: 5% Dextrose in water
options.C: 3.0% Sodium Chloride
options.D: 0.45% Sodium Chloride

explanation: Normal Saline at 0.9% concentration matches body fluid osmolarity, keeping red blood cells stable while expanding blood volume. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T16#GNS122_U1_T16_h3)

question: Your syringe driver beeps with an occlusion alarm. What is the very first thing you should check?

options.A: If the room lights are turned on brightly
options.B: Whether the extension tubing is kinked or clamped
options.C: Whether the pharmacy has new medication orders
options.D: If the patient's blood pressure is stable

explanation: Exactly right! Tracing the tubing to look for a bend, twist, or closed clamp usually fixes an occlusion alarm in seconds.

question: In clinical practice, what is a 'near-miss'?

options.A: A patient complaint about hospital food quality
options.B: A successful medical procedure completed quickly
options.C: An unplanned event that does not reach the patient
options.D: An error that causes permanent injury to a patient

explanation: You've got this! A near-miss is a close call—an error almost happened, but someone caught it just in time before it touched the patient.

question: Why is talking about birth control options right after a medical abortion so important?

options.A: It stops abnormal uterine bleeding from starting.
options.B: It helps prevent rapid repeat unintended pregnancies.
options.C: It prevents the uterus from contracting too forcefully.
options.D: It ensures that fertility returns safely after six months.

explanation: You nailed it! Because ovulation can happen as early as two weeks after an abortion, discussing contraception early helps patients avoid unplanned pregnancies before they are ready.

question: Why should a nurse check the formulary before giving a drug to a patient?

options.A: To find out which commercial brand name is the most expensive
options.B: To calculate the daily profit margin of the hospital pharmacy department
options.C: To verify normal dosage ranges and check for potential adverse reactions
options.D: To order new stock supplies directly from foreign manufacturers

explanation: Checking first is a great habit! It helps you confirm the safe dose and watch out for side effects before administration.

question: According to the Ann Arbor staging system, what defines Stage III lymphoma?

options.A: Spread to distant organs like the liver
options.B: Lymph node involvement on both sides of the diaphragm
options.C: Disease found only in the tummy area
options.D: Involvement of just a single lymph node

explanation: Think of the diaphragm as a dividing line. Stage III means enlarged nodes are hanging out both above AND below that breathing muscle.

question: How does water pollution directly hurt everyday communities?

options.A: By speeding up the natural flow of underground aquifers
options.B: By lowering the overall temperature of local rivers
options.C: By increasing the mineral content of drinking water
options.D: By making available water sources unsafe for daily use

explanation: You got it! When water is contaminated, families can no longer use it safely for drinking, cooking, or basic hygiene, posing an immediate health threat.

question: What is the main job of the ascending nerve tracts passing through the brain stem?

options.A: Coordinating balance with the cerebellum
options.B: Carrying sensory signals up to the brain
options.C: Producing automatic breathing rhythms
options.D: Transmitting motor orders down to muscles

explanation: Remember that 'ascending' means going up! These tracts carry sensory information from your body all the way up to higher brain areas.

question: Why must a stroke client pass a swallow test before you give them normal food?

options.A: To check if the client has an allergy to hospital cutlery
options.B: To prevent food from entering the airway and causing aspiration pneumonia
options.C: To ensure the stomach can digest heavy proteins and fats
options.D: To find out which specific food flavors the client prefers to eat

explanation: Stroke weakness can make throat muscles sluggish, meaning food or water can easily slip down the 'wrong pipe' into the lungs instead of the belly.

question: What usually causes a 'Check Pads' error message to pop up on a defibrillator screen?

options.A: Poor skin contact or loose cable connections
options.B: The patient has an implanted cardiac pacemaker
options.C: The room oxygen level is dangerously high
options.D: The battery is completely charged to maximum capacity

explanation: A 'Check Pads' warning simply means the machine isn't sensing a clean electrical connection with the skin. Check your leads and pad placement!

question: What makes a patient outcome goal measurable in a care plan?

options.A: It includes specific criteria like pain scores or timeline targets
options.B: It is written only by the attending physician
options.C: It states that the patient will feel better eventually
options.D: It relies entirely on the nurse's personal opinion

explanation: You got it! Measurable goals use clear indicators—like a specific pain scale number or a timeframe—so you can easily tell if the patient is improving.

question: What is an important nursing duty right after a client finishes their EEG?

options.A: Ensuring regular seizure medications are resumed promptly
options.B: Keeping the client awake for another twelve hours
options.C: Restricting oral fluid intake to prevent water intoxication
options.D: Applying fresh adhesive paste back onto the scalp

explanation: If any regular meds (especially seizure meds) were paused for the test, make sure to get them back on board right away to keep the patient safe!

question: Why is a team approach involving different professions so important when helping trafficking survivors?

options.A: Doctors are legally barred from talking to police officers
options.B: No single profession has all the skills needed for complex recovery
options.C: Legal frameworks prevent nurses from providing basic medical care
options.D: Psychological counseling is the only treatment survivors require

explanation: Trafficked children have diverse medical, emotional, and legal needs that require different experts working together seamlessly.

question: Which of these is NOT a recommended strategy for community nurses working in areas with traditional healing systems?

options.A: Advocating for the human rights of confined patients
options.B: Facilitating safe referrals to psychiatric facilities
options.C: Educating healers to spot severe mental illness signs
options.D: Condemning and mocking local cultural beliefs openly

explanation: You got this! Mocking cultural beliefs alienates the community and drives patients far away from seeking professional help. Always lead with respect.

question: What usually causes secondary traumatic stress in nursing?

options.A: Inadequate hospital parking space for clinical staff
options.B: Frequent changes in hospital uniform colors
options.C: Physical injuries sustained from heavy lifting in the ward
options.D: The emotional burden of listening to and caring for trauma survivors

explanation: Caring has a weight to it. When we constantly absorb the trauma stories of our patients, it can start to weigh heavily on our own minds.

question: What is the main sign of a post-dural puncture headache?

options.A: It worsens when the patient sits or stands up
options.B: It disappears completely after eating a meal
options.C: It only affects the left side of the forehead
options.D: It is accompanied by sudden high fever

explanation: Brilliant! When the patient sits up, the low fluid pressure pulls on sensitive head structures—making it hurt worse until they lie flat again.

question: Why can unending, chronic stress eventually lead to long-term anxiety or panic?

options.A: Because the muscles permanently lose their ability to relax
options.B: Because repeated stress sensitizes the brain's fear circuits
options.C: Because the liver stops producing essential blood proteins
options.D: Because chronic worry completely destroys all brain neurons

explanation: When your brain's alarm system stays switched on for too long without a break, those fear pathways get stuck on high alert. That's neuroplasticity working against us!

question: What does cross-contamination mean when keeping a diet gluten-free?

options.A: Safe food coming into physical contact with gluten-containing surfaces or utensils
options.B: The natural mutation of gluten proteins inside harvested grains
options.C: The chemical breakdown of proteins during high-heat baking
options.D: Mixing different types of safe gluten-free grains in one storage container

explanation: Cross-contamination happens when tiny bits of gluten accidentally transfer from a dirty counter, knife, or pan onto a safe meal.

question: A patient with a severe drug overdose has lost consciousness and normal gag reflexes. Why is intubation urgently required here?

options.A: To protect the lungs from choking on stomach contents
options.B: To reverse the chemical effects of the drug quickly
options.C: To increase blood flow to the brain tissue
options.D: To lower the patient's elevated body temperature

explanation: Unconscious patients lose protective airway reflexes, putting them at high risk of aspirating vomit into their lungs, which intubation prevents. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h1)

question: What is the first physical action a nurse should take when non-reassuring foetal heart patterns appear?

options.A: Change the mother's position to her side
options.B: Prepare the operating room for a caesarean section
options.C: Administer a strong dose of pain medication
options.D: Encourage the mother to push with all her strength

explanation: Turning the mother to her side takes pressure off major blood vessels, instantly improving blood return to the heart and placental blood flow. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T003#GNS226_U4_T003_h5)

question: A patient's lab results show a high neutrophil count. What does this usually point to?

options.A: An active internal hemorrhage
options.B: A chronic viral illness
options.C: An acute bacterial infection
options.D: A severe lack of dietary iron

explanation: Neutrophils are your front-line soldiers against bacteria. When an acute bacterial infection strikes, their numbers shoot up rapidly to defend the body.

question: A toddler in a home suffers skin burns from a pot of hot soup on the floor. What kind of accident is this?

options.A: An occupational accident
options.B: A domestic accident
options.C: A road traffic accident
options.D: An industrial accident

explanation: Mishaps like burns, cuts, and falls that happen right inside or around the home environment are called domestic accidents.

question: When checking a patient's walking stick (cane) or walker, what is the most important thing for you as a nurse to verify?

options.A: Instructing the patient to use it only during nighttime hours
options.B: Ensuring the device is the correct height and in good repair
options.C: Painting the frame a bright color so it looks modern
options.D: Replacing the assistive device with a wheelchair immediately

explanation: A worn-out or poorly adjusted walking aid can actually cause unsteadiness and lead to another fall. Always check the height and rubber tips!

question: Which of the following is classified strictly as sharps waste?

options.A: Used hypodermic needles
options.B: Expired paracetamol tablets
options.C: Discarded surgical gloves
options.D: Soiled cotton swabs

explanation: Needles, blades, and any objects capable of causing punctures or cuts fall under the category of sharps waste. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h2)

question: During birth, the baby's chin tucks tightly against its chest. What is this movement called?

options.A: Flexion
options.B: Extension
options.C: Descent
options.D: Restitution

explanation: That tucking action is called flexion! It helps the smallest part of the baby's head lead the way through the pelvis.

question: How do mass movements differ from regular mixing movements in the large intestine?

options.A: Segmental movements require conscious effort to move waste.
options.B: Segmental contractions happen only once or twice a day.
options.C: Mass movements push stool a long way toward the rectum all at once.
options.D: Mass movements happen non-stop all day and night.

explanation: Mass movements are like big, powerful waves that sweep through the colon every now and then to clear out stored waste toward the exit. You've got this!

question: What is the main reason we wash our hands before preparing food?

options.A: To activate natural sweat gland secretions
options.B: To prevent transferring harmful microbes to food
options.C: To remove natural skin oils and improve grip
options.D: To cool down the hands before touching ingredients

explanation: Simple hand hygiene stops unseen germs on our skin from hitching a ride into the food and making people sick.

question: A rural maternity clinic keeps running out of oxytocin right when women are in active labor. What system failure does this point to?

options.A: Inadequate clinical assessment skills among the nursing staff
options.B: Lack of patient education on family planning methods
options.C: Poor supply chain management and resource allocation
options.D: Excessive compliance with evidence-based clinical guidelines

explanation: Spot on! Running out of life-saving drugs means there is a breakdown in how supplies are ordered, tracked, and delivered to the clinic. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T2#GNS312_U5_T2_h5)

question: Which of the following actions should NOT be done when managing a patient who has just fainted?

options.A: Force the patient to stand up immediately
options.B: Loosen tight clothing around the neck
options.C: Elevate the lower legs slightly
options.D: Assess the airway and breathing

explanation: Forcing a recently fainted person to stand up will pull blood back down to the legs and cause another faint. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T16#GNS123_U3_T16_h6)

question: Why is it important to talk about pain management before the patient takes misoprostol?

options.A: Pain medications must be taken to prevent allergic reactions to the drug
options.B: Analgesics speed up the absorption of the hormone in the stomach lining
options.C: Misoprostol causes strong uterine contractions that lead to significant cramping
options.D: Pain medication stops the excessive bleeding that occurs right away

explanation: Cramping is a very normal part of the process because the uterus is working hard to empty. Planning ahead for pain relief keeps our patients comfortable!

question: Which drug class is most commonly linked to increased fall risk due to central nervous system depression?

options.A: Topical skin antibiotics
options.B: Sedatives and hypnotics
options.C: Inhaled respiratory bronchodilators
options.D: Oral vitamin supplements

explanation: Sedatives slow down brain activity, causing drowsiness, reduced alertness, and poor coordination that easily leads to a fall. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T5#GNS324_U6_T5_h4)

question: When should a nurse apply standard precautions during patient care?

options.A: When working exclusively in surgical operating theaters
options.B: Only after a laboratory confirms a bloodborne pathogen
options.C: Only when caring for patients with confirmed viral infections
options.D: During the care of all patients regardless of their diagnosis

explanation: Standard precautions treat all body fluids as potentially infectious and must be used for every patient every time. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T95#GNS214_U1_T95_h4)

question: Why is showing empathy such a powerful tool in community nursing?

options.A: It eliminates the need to document nursing assessments.
options.B: It encourages patients to share sensitive information they might otherwise hide.
options.C: It guarantees that the patient will never experience chronic illness.
options.D: It allows the nurse to take over complete legal control of the household.

explanation: When patients feel safe and unjudged, they'll open up about the real struggles they face with their health. Empathy wins every time!

question: In the Three Delays Model for maternal mortality, what does the second delay mean?

options.A: Postponing antenatal care visits until the third trimester of pregnancy
options.B: Reaching a functioning health facility due to transport and distance problems
options.C: Deciding whether or not to leave the home when labor contractions start
options.D: Waiting for doctors to arrive at the hospital after the patient has registered

explanation: The second delay is all about logistics—navigating bad roads, lack of vehicles, and long distances to get a patient to a clinic or hospital. Spot-on!

question: Which of these is most likely to make people refuse to join a community insurance scheme?

options.A: A lack of trust in the managers handling the funds
options.B: Excessive availability of free medication
options.C: Too many doctors working in local health clinics
options.D: High levels of income among farmers

explanation: Trust is everything! If community members don't trust the people managing the money, they simply won't invest their hard-earned cash into the health scheme.

question: How do nurses primarily bridge the gap between public health policy and the local community?

options.A: By manufacturing pharmaceuticals in industrial laboratory settings
options.B: By working directly with individuals and families as educators and care providers
options.C: By writing national healthcare laws and passing public health budgets
options.D: By managing international trade agreements for medical supplies

explanation: Spot on! Nurses interact face-to-face with community members every day, making them the best messengers for public health guidelines.

question: Why does the pregnant body develop natural insulin resistance in the later stages of gestation?

options.A: To speed up the digestion of dietary fats and proteins
options.B: To keep more glucose circulating in the blood for fetal uptake
options.C: To help the pancreas rest from producing digestive enzymes
options.D: To prevent the mother from ever developing type 2 diabetes

explanation: Insulin resistance ensures that less glucose is used by maternal tissues, making more available in the bloodstream to cross the placenta for the baby. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h4)

question: When a medical error happens, who is commonly referred to as the "second victim"?

options.A: The family member who witnessed the event
options.B: The hospital administrator in charge
options.C: The patient who suffered the primary injury
options.D: The healthcare provider involved in the event

explanation: Even though the patient is the primary victim, the nurse or doctor involved often carries heavy emotional or psychological trauma afterwards. We call them the second victim. Don't worry, it's completely normal to feel shaken, and you're doing great learning about this!

question: What is a bone fracture?

options.A: A stretching injury to skeletal muscle fibers
options.B: A severe infection inside the bone marrow
options.C: A complete tearing of a ligament near a joint
options.D: A break or disruption in the continuity of a bone

explanation: Simple and clear! A fracture just means the bone's structure has cracked or broken. You've got this!

question: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of descriptive research?

options.A: Generating useful baseline data for future studies
options.B: Providing a clear picture of health habits in a community
options.C: Proving definitively which nursing intervention cures chronic illness
options.D: Being relatively fast and cost-effective to carry out

explanation: Descriptive research is great for painting a picture or saving time and money, but proving a cure requires heavy-duty experimental trials! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h7)

question: Which detail is NOT required when documenting a new peripheral IV insertion?

options.A: The catheter gauge and anatomical location
options.B: The brand name of the soap used for handwashing
options.C: The patient's response and tolerance to the procedure
options.D: The date and exact time of the insertion

explanation: Standard hand hygiene is assumed; charting focuses on the specific procedure details like size, location, time, and patient response. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h10)

question: Why are folk media like traditional drama and local songs so effective in rural communities?

options.A: They require expensive electronic equipment and stable electricity to function
options.B: They focus strictly on complex medical terminology and research data
options.C: They eliminate the need for nurses to speak to the community directly
options.D: They connect deeply with local culture and engage audiences who may not read well

explanation: Using familiar cultural practices makes health messages fun and accessible to everyone in the community, regardless of literacy.

question: What is the main goal of antiretroviral therapy (ART) for adolescents living with HIV?

options.A: To suppress viral replication and preserve immune function
options.B: To stimulate appetite and cause weight gain
options.C: To replace damaged bone marrow cells permanently
options.D: To cure the infection completely within a few weeks

explanation: You got it! ART keeps the virus levels super low, allowing the immune system to stay strong and protect the body.

question: What are the main warning signs of severe pre-eclampsia during pregnancy?

options.A: Complete cessation of fetal movements felt by the mother for two days
options.B: Very high blood pressure accompanied by severe headache and visual changes
options.C: Sudden painless vaginal bleeding in the third trimester of pregnancy
options.D: High fever with generalized body chills and offensive vaginal discharge

explanation: Always watch out for high blood pressure paired with stubborn headaches or blurred vision—these are big red flags for pre-eclampsia!

question: Which category do single-use items like gauze and disposable syringes fall under?

options.A: Emergency pharmaceuticals
options.B: Durable equipment
options.C: Consumables
options.D: Controlled substances

explanation: Consumables are those handy everyday items designed to be used just once for a patient and then safely discarded.

question: When is it legally and ethically okay to use physical restraints or seclusion on a ward?

options.A: When the ward is short-staffed and busy
options.B: If the patient refuses to participate in group therapy
options.C: Whenever the nursing shift changes in the morning
options.D: When the patient is an immediate danger to self or others

explanation: Restraints are an absolute last resort. We only use them to keep the patient and everyone around them safe from immediate physical harm.

question: How do poor internet and lack of journal access affect local nursing research?

options.A: They prevent nurses from wearing their uniforms to work
options.B: They force patients to travel abroad for medical treatments
options.C: They increase the number of medication errors in the wards
options.D: They make thorough literature reviews and data analysis very difficult

explanation: Spot on. Without good internet access, checking what other researchers around the world have discovered becomes a massive struggle.

question: A nurse notices a sudden jump in malaria cases during the rainy season. What kind of transmission is this?

options.A: Foodborne
options.B: Waterborne
options.C: Vector-borne
options.D: Airborne

explanation: Spot on! Malaria is spread by mosquitoes (the vector), which love to breed in the puddles formed during the rainy season.

question: In research, what does the term 'reliability' mean?

options.A: Whether the tool measures what it is supposed to measure
options.B: The speed at which the patient answers interview questions
options.C: Consistency of results when using a tool repeatedly
options.D: How expensive the laboratory equipment is to purchase

explanation: Spot on! If a tool is reliable, it gives you stable, dependable results every time you use it under the same conditions.

question: What is the main job of the 'memory cells' created when someone gets vaccinated?

options.A: To permanently alter the person's genetic DNA structure
options.B: To destroy healthy tissue to make space for white blood cells
options.C: To slow down the immune response to prevent inflammation
options.D: To provide a rapid and strong defense upon future exposure to the germ

explanation: Exactly! Memory cells never forget a face; they spot the real germ later in life and fight it off instantly.

question: What is the key difference between monitoring and evaluating an IEC campaign?

options.A: Monitoring is done by doctors, while evaluation is done exclusively by government auditors.
options.B: Monitoring happens after the campaign ends, while evaluation happens before printing.
options.C: Monitoring tracks distribution activities, while evaluation measures actual health outcomes and behavior changes.
options.D: Monitoring looks at money spent, while evaluation looks at paper quality.

explanation: Think of monitoring as tracking your daily steps during the campaign, while evaluation checks the final results and lifestyle changes at the end.

question: Which group of vitamins is known as fat-soluble?

options.A: Vitamins A, D, E, and K
options.B: Vitamin C and the B-complex group
options.C: Calcium, iron, and potassium
options.D: Amino acids and plant extracts

explanation: Think of vitamins A, D, E, and K as the ones that dissolve in fat and can hang out in our body's fatty tissues and liver for later use.

question: Why is it important for a nurse manager to understand their hospital's chain of command?

options.A: To ensure that nurses never participate in patient care decisions
options.B: To guarantee that the hospital operates as a simple structure
options.C: To avoid having to communicate with any physicians or doctors
options.D: To effectively navigate reporting lines and advocate for resources

explanation: Knowing who to talk to up the ladder helps nurse managers solve problems quickly, speak up for their ward, and get needed supplies.

question: What happens when clinic staff guess tally counts on extremely busy days?

options.A: It leads to distorted health statistics that misguide national disease planning and resource allocation.
options.B: It causes client folders to physically deteriorate faster.
options.C: It automatically increases the clinic budget allocation.
options.D: It results in the immediate suspension of the senior nurse.

explanation: Guessed data leads to bad government decisions. If the numbers say you treated 50 kids for malaria when it was actually 500, the next drug supply shipment will be way too small!

question: Why is the PDSA cycle so helpful in Nigerian healthcare settings with limited resources?

options.A: It allows nurses to test low-cost workflow changes without needing massive budgets
options.B: It forces the federal government to build new hospitals in every rural town
options.C: It automatically provides millions of naira in foreign grants to the hospital
options.D: It prevents nurses from ever having to deal with power outages or shortages

explanation: Brilliant! You don't need a huge budget to improve care. PDSA helps us make smart, practical changes with what we already have.

question: What is the specialized name for the plasma membrane of a skeletal muscle fiber?

options.A: Sarcoplasmic reticulum
options.B: Sarcoplasm
options.C: Sarcolemma
options.D: Sarcomere

explanation: The sarcolemma is the cell membrane surrounding a skeletal muscle fiber. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h3)

question: A patient suffers a stroke in the left motor cortex of the brain. Where will the resulting muscle weakness appear?

options.A: Only in the muscles of the face
options.B: On the right side of the body
options.C: Equally on both sides of the body
options.D: On the left side of the body

explanation: Because motor fibers cross at the medullary pyramids, damage to one side of the brain affects the contralateral side of the body. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a good safety practice for emergency equipment?

options.A: Conducting regular staff simulation drills
options.B: Ignoring minor device malfunctions
options.C: Documenting equipment maintenance logs
options.D: Debriefing team performance after code events

explanation: Spot on! Never brush off small faults—minor issues can turn into big failures during a real emergency. Keep up the great work! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h5)

question: Why do nursing schools connect classroom lectures with clinical ward postings?

options.A: To help you apply what you read in textbooks to real patients
options.B: To cut down the number of hours you spend in school
options.C: To replace tests with chats by the patient's bedside
options.D: To keep students away from the school campus

explanation: Bridging theory and practice helps you understand the real 'why' behind the bedside care you give to your patients.

question: Which symptom is a common physical sign of high stress?

options.A: Complete paralysis of the limbs
options.B: Uncontrollable tremors in the legs
options.C: Muscle tension and headaches
options.D: Joint swelling and redness

explanation: When stressed, we often clench our muscles without realizing it, which frequently leads to tight shoulders, sore muscles, and tension headaches.

question: Which cells in the stomach lining make and release hydrochloric acid?

options.A: Chief cells
options.B: Parietal cells
options.C: Endocrine cells
options.D: Mucous cells

explanation: Parietal cells are the acid-pumpers of the stomach, releasing both hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor to help with digestion.

question: What is the main purpose of a formal grievance procedure in a hospital?

options.A: To give management an easy excuse to fire disobedient nurses
options.B: To determine which staff members deserve annual promotion
options.C: To resolve staff complaints fairly without fear of victimization
options.D: To bypass national labour laws during salary negotiations

explanation: A grievance procedure is a safe, official channel where staff can voice complaints or resolve workplace issues without worrying that management will punish them for speaking up.

question: What is a major danger of misusing drugs in healthcare settings?

options.A: Immediate reduction in the overall cost of running hospitals
options.B: Development of antimicrobial resistance to common infections
options.C: Faster recovery times for patients with chronic illnesses
options.D: Decreased workload for nurses on the hospital wards

explanation: When we overuse antibiotics, germs learn how to fight back and survive, making common infections much harder to treat later.

question: Why is it unhelpful to just write off a family planning defaulter as simply 'uncooperative'?

options.A: It guarantees the patient will never return to the facility
options.B: It breaks hospital regulations regarding patient confidentiality
options.C: It automatically makes the client pregnant within a week
options.D: It ignores practical barriers and personal reasons driving the missed appointment

explanation: People miss appointments for real reasons—like side effects, transport costs, or busy schedules. Looking past the label helps us solve the actual problem together.

question: What is the key sign that tells normal aging apart from a serious brain decline?

options.A: Preferring quiet activities over large social gatherings
options.B: Interference with daily functioning and independence
options.C: Needing reading glasses to see small text clearly
options.D: A slight increase in overall wisdom and life experience

explanation: When memory slips start getting in the way of daily living and safety, that crosses into pathological decline. Spotting this is a key nursing skill!

question: What should day care staff do when they notice a child showing signs of a developmental delay?

options.A: Scold the child for failing to meet peer standards
options.B: Ignore the sign until the child starts primary school
options.C: Withhold meals until the developmental milestone is met
options.D: Note the observation and refer the family for assessment

explanation: Early identification and referral help ensure children get the professional support they need for developmental delays. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h5)

question: Which of these is a very common cause of weakened pelvic floor muscles in women?

options.A: Vaginal childbirth
options.B: Regular aerobic exercise
options.C: Eating high-fiber foods
options.D: Drinking too much water

explanation: The stretching and hard work of vaginal delivery can tire out or stretch the pelvic floor support structures, making leaks more likely later on.

question: After putting glaucoma eye drops in a patient, what quick action stops the medicine from entering the rest of the body?

options.A: Wipe the outer eyelids firmly with an alcohol swab
options.B: Tell the patient to blink rapidly twenty times
options.C: Cover both eyes with a thick pressure bandage
options.D: Apply gentle pressure to the inner corner near the tear duct

explanation: Gentle pressure on the inner corner (nasolacrimal occlusion) blocks the drop from draining down into the nose and entering the bloodstream. Smart nursing care!

question: Why do public health nurses look at mental health through a collective lens rather than just an individual one?

options.A: A person's state of mind is deeply connected to their environment and living conditions
options.B: Individual therapy sessions are too expensive for community clinics to fund
options.C: Group counseling is the only proven method to treat depression
options.D: Government policies require nurses to ignore personal medical histories

explanation: Because people are influenced by their surroundings, housing, and social networks, community nurses must evaluate the broader environment to understand mental well-being. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T7#GNS314_U1_T7_h1)

question: Which of the following is a major ethical concern when using electronic health records?

options.A: The physical weight of computer monitors on the ward
options.B: The cost of buying ink for hospital printers
options.C: The bright lighting of phone screens in dark rooms
options.D: Patient privacy and data security risks

explanation: Protecting confidential health information from unauthorized access or cyber threats is a primary ethical duty for all nurses. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h7)

question: In the PDSA cycle, during which phase does the nurse actually carry out the proposed change on a small scale?

options.A: Act phase
options.B: Plan phase
options.C: Study phase
options.D: Do phase

explanation: Keep it up! The 'Do' phase is where you roll up your sleeves and try out the new idea on a small scale to see how it feels in practice.

question: What happens during the 'tonic' phase of a seizure?

options.A: Rapid wandering around the room
options.B: Sudden return of normal alertness
options.C: Sudden stiffening of the body muscles
options.D: Total relaxation and limpness of limbs

explanation: You got it! Think of 'tonic' as 'tone' or stiffness—the body goes rigid abruptly.

question: What is the standard rule for turning a bed-bound patient to help prevent pressure sores?

options.A: Every two hours
options.B: Every six hours
options.C: Once per shift
options.D: Only when they complain of pain

explanation: Turning a patient at least every two hours takes the weight off vulnerable spots, giving blood flow a chance to rush back in and save the skin. Simple and life-saving! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h6)

question: What do the double upward arrows on a medical shipping box mean?

options.A: The temperature range required inside the shipping compartment
options.B: The correct upright orientation to prevent liquid leaks
options.C: The maximum stacking limit allowed for storage in the warehouse
options.D: The direction the delivery vehicle must drive to reach the lab

explanation: Those arrows must point straight up so the liquid tubes inside stay upright and don't leak through their caps. Good clinical detail to know!

question: When your clinical teacher watches you perform a sterile wound dressing, which domain of learning are they checking?

options.A: Theoretical memory recall
options.B: Cognitive domain only
options.C: Psychomotor domain
options.D: Affective domain exclusively

explanation: Dressing a wound is a physical, hands-on procedure, which falls squarely into the psychomotor domain. Hands-on practice makes perfect!

question: When can palliative care start for someone diagnosed with cancer?

options.A: At the time of diagnosis alongside curative treatment
options.B: Only when all chemotherapy and radiation have failed
options.C: Strictly during the final twenty-four hours of life
options.D: Only after the patient is discharged to hospice care

explanation: Palliative care isn't just for the end of life—it can start right away to help manage symptoms and keep the patient comfortable while fighting the disease.

question: Why does fluid build up in the ventricles in a patient with obstructive hydrocephalus caused by a brain tumor?

options.A: A physical mass is blocking the normal outflow channels of the ventricular system
options.B: The arachnoid villi are working too efficiently and pulling out too much blood
options.C: The brain cells are suddenly manufacturing ten times more fluid than normal
options.D: The cranial bones are expanding too fast for the fluid to fill the space

explanation: Exactly right! When a tumor or mass physically blocks the narrow drainage paths, the fluid gets trapped upstream, causing pressure to rise.

question: Why do patriarchal community norms negatively affect child health outcomes?

options.A: They restrict mothers from making independent medical choices for sick children
options.B: They encourage mothers to lead community health committees
options.C: They force fathers to spend all their income on infant vaccines
options.D: They automatically increase the nutritional value of local foods

explanation: When mothers lack household authority, they cannot easily take a sick child to the clinic without prior approval from male heads. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T59#GNS214_U1_T59_h4)

question: Why is teaching sleep hygiene so important in recovery?

options.A: It replaces the need for any nutritional counseling
options.B: It guarantees that the patient will never feel tired again
options.C: It helps regulate rest patterns to restore depleted nervous energy
options.D: It cures underlying infectious diseases

explanation: You're doing great! Good sleep habits give the tired nervous system the deep rest it needs to repair itself. Keep practicing daily!

question: Why is it recommended to gently press on the tragus after instilling ear drops?

options.A: It prevents earwax from hardening further
options.B: It warms up the liquid drops inside the canal
options.C: It helps move the medication down into the ear canal
options.D: It seals the ear completely to block out loud noises

explanation: Pumping the tragus gently creates a mild suction effect that helps the drops travel down the canal toward the eardrum. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h6)

question: What is a top clinical priority when caring for a patient mid-flight?

options.A: Adjusting the aircraft navigation controls
options.B: Maintaining airway security and hemodynamic stability
options.C: Serving meals and beverages to the transport crew
options.D: Completing billing forms before landing

explanation: Spot on, nurse! Keeping the airway clear and vital signs stable will always be your number one duty in any critical transport.

question: Why is the urinary bladder easily injured when someone has a pelvic fracture?

options.A: Pelvic fractures cause the bladder to instantly rupture from high pressure.
options.B: The bladder is located completely outside the bony pelvis.
options.C: Fractures stop blood flow to the bladder, causing tissue death.
options.D: Sharp broken edges of the pelvic bones can puncture the bladder wall.

explanation: Think of the bladder resting right behind the pubic bone. When that bone breaks, the sharp edges can easily poke or tear the bladder next to it. Simple and logical!

question: When we talk about 'psychosocial' care in mental health nursing, what two main things are we bringing together?

options.A: Laboratory values and physical symptoms
options.B: Emotional experiences and environmental conditions
options.C: Surgical history and genetic mutations
options.D: Medication side effects and dietary habits

explanation: Spot on! Psychosocial care looks at both sides of the coin: what is happening inside a person's mind (psychological) and what is happening in their world outside (social).

question: What is a critical rule to follow regarding promises made to disaster survivors?

options.A: Promise that all their family members are safe
options.B: Tell them the government will pay for everything
options.C: Never make promises you cannot guarantee to keep
options.D: Promise them a new home to make them feel better

explanation: False promises destroy trust and increase anxiety when reality turns out differently. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T6#GNS315_U5_T6_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of a health referral system?

options.A: To generate more revenue for large tertiary hospitals
options.B: To prevent patients from ever visiting traditional healers
options.C: To reduce the number of staff needed at rural health posts
options.D: To move patients smoothly between different levels of care

explanation: A referral system connects basic clinics with advanced hospitals to ensure continuous and appropriate patient care. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h1)

question: What is the main goal of doing an occupational health hazard assessment?

options.A: To identify and evaluate potential health and safety risks
options.B: To discipline workers who fail to wear uniforms
options.C: To check the company's financial profits and losses
options.D: To prescribe medications for non-work illnesses

explanation: The main point of a hazard assessment is to spot dangerous conditions early so we can protect workers before anyone gets hurt.

question: What does it mean if a placenta is described as a 'battledore placenta'?

options.A: A placenta with a thick white ring on its edge
options.B: A placenta split into two equal-sized lobes
options.C: A placenta where the umbilical cord inserts at the margin
options.D: A placenta with an accessory lobe nearby

explanation: Think of a battledore insertion like a tennis racket handle attached right at the edge of the disk instead of the middle. Easy to picture once you see it! [learn more](GNS121_U6_T6#GNS121_U6_T6_h2)

question: What is the main reason for adding pressure support to a patient who is already breathing on their own through a ventilator?

options.A: To paralyze the respiratory muscles during painful procedures
options.B: To help overcome the resistance of the artificial airway
options.C: To completely take over the work of breathing for the patient
options.D: To measure the exact lung compliance of the patient

explanation: Breathing through a narrow plastic tube is tough work! Pressure support gives a gentle push to make it easier for the patient to draw air through the tube.

question: What kind of pressure is normally found inside the healthy pleural space around the lungs?

options.A: Atmospheric pressure
options.B: Fluctuating pressure
options.C: Positive pressure
options.D: Negative pressure

explanation: Great job! The pleural space naturally acts like a vacuum (negative pressure) to keep our lungs nicely expanded against the chest wall.

question: Why is investing in better pay and working conditions for health workers crucial for a country?

options.A: It forces hospitals to close down unprofitable departments.
options.B: It increases the cost of basic medicines for patients.
options.C: It eliminates the need for primary healthcare centers.
options.D: It encourages skilled staff to stay and reduces brain drain.

explanation: Good salaries and stable working environments give health professionals a reason to remain in their home country, keeping hospitals staffed and functional. [learn more](GST322_U3_T7#GST322_U3_T7_h6)

question: Which airway opening technique should you use if you suspect a neck injury in a cardiac arrest patient?

options.A: Lateral recovery position
options.B: Jaw-thrust maneuver
options.C: Head-tilt, chin-lift maneuver
options.D: Neck-hyperextension technique

explanation: Safety first! The jaw-thrust lets you open the airway without bending or moving the neck, keeping the cervical spine safe in trauma cases.

question: In many Nigerian homes, who is often involved when making healthcare decisions for an elderly patient?

options.A: Only the youngest child living in the household
options.B: Extended family networks and community elders
options.C: Foreign medical tourism agencies exclusively
options.D: The neighborhood security guards on duty

explanation: Spot on! Healthcare decisions in our local settings are often communal, bringing in extended family members and respected elders to support the patient.

question: If a nurse researcher tests patients with a pain scale twice, why is a very short time interval between tests sometimes a bad idea?

options.A: The patients will experience severe physical exhaustion
options.B: Hospital management will not approve the extra paperwork
options.C: Patients might remember and repeat their previous answers
options.D: The thermometer or scale will lose its electrical charge

explanation: This is called recall bias! If patients just remember what they wrote five minutes ago, they'll copy it, making the tool look more reliable than it actually is.

question: What can a patient do using a patient portal connected to a hospital EHR?

options.A: It allows patients to view lab results and message their care team online
options.B: It gives hospital administrators access to employee payroll records
options.C: It lets patients perform emergency surgical procedures on themselves
options.D: It replaces the physical bedside nurse during hospital admissions

explanation: Spot on! Patient portals empower patients to check their own lab results and chat with their nurses and doctors online.

question: What is the main purpose of fructose found in seminal vesicle secretions?

options.A: It lubricates the walls of the vas deferens
options.B: It acts as a primary energy source for moving sperm
options.C: It kills harmful bacteria inside the urethra
options.D: It neutralizes the acidic environment of the vagina

explanation: Sperm use the fructose sugar secreted by the seminal vesicles to power their flagella for swimming. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T3#GNS121_U4_T3_h2)

question: Which of these is counted as a healthy food group in standard dietary scoring?

options.A: Dark green leafy vegetables
options.B: Carbonated soft drinks
options.C: Processed table sugar
options.D: Artificial food flavorings

explanation: That's right! Ugwu, spinach, and other dark greens are packed with essential nutrients like iron and folate to keep the body strong.

question: What do we mean by the 'halo effect' when grading students?

options.A: Using computer software to grade practical nursing procedures
options.B: Failing to evaluate a student due to a lack of time on the ward
options.C: Giving every student a failing grade because of one minor mistake
options.D: Allowing one positive trait of a student to unfairly influence the entire evaluation

explanation: The halo effect happens when a student's polite smile or charm makes an instructor overlook their clinical mistakes. We want objective grading!

question: Why should a nurse check the blood count (hemoglobin and hematocrit) of a patient with large fibroids?

options.A: To screen for anemia caused by heavy menstrual bleeding
options.B: To determine if the patient has reached menopause
options.C: To measure the exact weight of the growing tumors
options.D: To calculate the correct dose of oral contraceptives

explanation: Heavy monthly bleeding from fibroids often drains iron stores, so checking for anemia is a key nursing assessment.

question: How does qualitative data analysis differ from quantitative analysis?

options.A: Qualitative analysis looks for recurring themes in text rather than numbers
options.B: Qualitative analysis ignores patient words and focuses on lab values
options.C: Qualitative analysis uses computer software to run complex regressions
options.D: Qualitative analysis requires strict mathematical proof of significance

explanation: Instead of crunching numbers, qualitative researchers read through text to find common patterns and themes in what people said.

question: Why must public health measures continue even if a disease is wiped out in Nigeria?

options.A: Local health workers lose their medical licenses after an outbreak
options.B: The pathogen can still be imported from other regions where it exists
options.C: Patients will develop allergies if vaccination programs stop
options.D: Eliminated diseases always mutate into completely different organisms

explanation: As long as the germ is active in other parts of the world, travelers or animals can easily bring it back across borders. Stay alert!

question: Why do nurses and dietitians use activity multipliers along with a patient's BMR?

options.A: To correct for errors in food label calorie counts
options.B: To determine the patient's exact vitamin requirements
options.C: To account for daily movement and exercise energy costs
options.D: To calculate the exact amount of daily water loss

explanation: BMR only covers resting in bed. Activity multipliers help us estimate the extra calories burned walking around or doing physical therapy.

question: Which part of the nervous system includes the sensory nerves branching out to your skin and organs?

options.A: Central nervous system
options.B: Peripheral nervous system
options.C: Autonomic sympathetic chain
options.D: Enteric digestive network

explanation: You got it! Think of the central nervous system as the main office (brain and spinal cord), while the peripheral nervous system is the field crew reaching out to every corner of the body.

question: Why does damage to the primary motor cortex on the right side of the brain cause weakness on the left side of the body?

options.A: The right side of the brain only controls internal organs
options.B: Motor pathways cross over to the opposite side of the body
options.C: Blood supply is shared equally between both body halves
options.D: Sensory nerves block motor signals from reaching the right limbs

explanation: Because of contralateral decussation, the motor cortex controls skeletal muscles on the opposite (contralateral) side of the body. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T10#GNS211_U3_T10_h2)

question: How do you calculate the basic range of a data set?

options.A: Dividing the sum of all values by the number of observations
options.B: Adding the highest value to the lowest value and dividing by two
options.C: Finding the difference between the upper and lower quartiles
options.D: Subtracting the lowest value from the highest value

explanation: The range is super easy to remember: just take the highest number and subtract the lowest number to see the total span!

question: You are filling out a referral form for a pregnant mum with severe pre-eclampsia. What is the most important clinical finding to write down?

options.A: Her personal opinion about hospital food quality
options.B: The distance from her house to the primary healthcare center
options.C: The name of her local community youth organization
options.D: Her most recent blood pressure reading and urine protein test

explanation: Brilliant! Vital signs like her BP and protein levels give the incoming delivery and doctor team immediate, life-saving information.

question: A woman who had FGM as a child comes in for delivery. What major complication is she most at risk for?

options.A: Complete absence of uterine contractions throughout the first stage
options.B: Obstructed labor due to severe scar tissue and rigid tissue narrowing
options.C: Sudden development of gestational diabetes mellitus
options.D: Premature closure of the infant's fontanelles inside the womb

explanation: Spot on! Thick scar tissue from FGM doesn't stretch easily, making it very hard for the baby to pass through smoothly during childbirth.

question: A ward has very sick patients and several junior nurses on duty. What is the best staffing approach?

options.A: Pair junior nurses with experienced senior nurses
options.B: Send all the junior nurses home to rest
options.C: Ignore the patient acuity levels when scheduling
options.D: Assign all critical patients to the most junior nurse

explanation: You got it! Teaming up junior nurses with experienced seniors keeps patients safe and helps the junior staff learn safely.

question: Which action is a serious legal violation in healthcare financial administration?

options.A: Reporting an unfavorable budget variance to the hospital director
options.B: Collaborating with finance officers to review monthly shift overtime
options.C: Documenting medical procedures that were never actually performed
options.D: Using generic brand dressings instead of expensive name brands

explanation: Falsifying records to boost hospital revenue is fraudulent and illegal. Integrity always comes first in nursing!

question: What is an essential first step for a nurse providing effective sexual health advocacy?

options.A: Overcoming personal discomfort and professional biases
options.B: Referring every patient directly to a psychiatric hospital
options.C: Writing research papers on rare reproductive diseases
options.D: Requiring patients to sign a formal intimacy contract

explanation: Nurses must first address their own biases and discomfort to create a safe, welcoming environment for their patients. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T26#GNS312_U1_T26_h8)

question: Why is occupational therapy so helpful for patients with chronic joint disorders?

options.A: It provides surgical joint replacement procedures
options.B: It teaches energy-conservation techniques and assistive devices
options.C: It cures the underlying autoimmune malfunction
options.D: It prescribes high-dose corticosteroid injections

explanation: Occupational therapists are wonderful! They teach patients smart ways to protect their joints, save energy, and use handy tools to stay independent.

question: What is the main focus of palliative care in a residential care home?

options.A: Discharging residents to an acute hospital ward immediately
options.B: Aggressive medical interventions to cure terminal chronic illnesses
options.C: Providing comfort, pain management, and dignity during end-of-life
options.D: Restricting family visits to maintain strict facility quiet hours

explanation: Brilliant! Palliative care is all about comforting patients, easing pain, and giving them dignity when curing is no longer possible.

question: How often should you check and record temperatures in a clinic's vaccine refrigerator?

options.A: Twice daily
options.B: Every hour
options.C: Only on weekends
options.D: Once a week

explanation: Checking temperatures twice a day helps us catch fridge issues early and keeps our vaccine supply safe for the community!

question: What is the main role of the nurse when working as part of an interprofessional healthcare team?

options.A: Performing all physical and occupational therapy sessions alone
options.B: Handling only the financial and discharge paperwork for the hospital
options.C: Overriding decisions made by physicians and therapists
options.D: Acting as the central coordinator who synthesizes updates from all disciplines

explanation: Because you are at the bedside around the clock, you bring together updates from doctors, therapists, and dietitians to keep everyone on the same page!

question: How does community mobilisation change the way local people take part in health programs?

options.A: It makes villagers responsible for hiring and firing doctors
options.B: It forces community members to fund all local clinic budgets
options.C: It turns passive recipients into active partners in health
options.D: It replaces the need for professional nurses in rural areas

explanation: You got it! Instead of just waiting for health workers to tell them what to do, mobilisation gets community members involved as active partners in their own wellbeing.

question: Why do many breast cancer patients in Nigeria sadly arrive at the hospital with advanced stages?

options.A: Mandatory waiting periods imposed by primary health clinics
options.B: Delays caused by financial barriers and reliance on traditional remedies
options.C: Strict government laws prohibiting early surgical intervention
options.D: Rapid genetic mutation rates exclusive to West African populations

explanation: Money constraints and trying out traditional or spiritual remedies first often delay proper medical care. As nurses, patient education is our superpower here!

question: When we classify joints by their 'function', what are we actually looking at?

options.A: The presence of a fluid-filled cavity
options.B: The type of tissue binding the bones
options.C: How much movement the joint allows
options.D: The specific shape of the bone ends

explanation: Great thinking! Functional classification simply looks at how much motion a joint gives you—whether it moves a lot, a little, or not at all.

question: Why do nurses apply universal precautions to every patient, not just those with a known infection?

options.A: Hospital management requires it to save money on lab testing
options.B: Testing blood takes too many days to be useful in an emergency
options.C: Many individuals with infections may be completely unaware or undiagnosed
options.D: Patients get offended if nurses ask about their infection status

explanation: Spot on! Many people carry bloodborne viruses without knowing it, so treating every patient's fluids as potentially infectious keeps everyone safe.

question: Which of these is a real-world factor that often shapes a healthcare manager's choices?

options.A: The color scheme of the hospital exterior
options.B: The weather forecast for the upcoming weekend
options.C: The astrological sign of the nurse manager
options.D: Resource availability and funding

explanation: What you have in terms of money, supplies, and available staff directly dictates what practical choices you can make.

question: A ward manager checks how often nurses wash their hands before doing wound dressings. What kind of indicator is this?

options.A: Balancing indicator
options.B: Outcome indicator
options.C: Process indicator
options.D: Structure indicator

explanation: Hand hygiene compliance measures how care is actually being carried out. That action falls right under process indicators!

question: What is the name of the tough, outermost protective layer that wraps around a whole spinal nerve?

options.A: Meninges
options.B: Epineurium
options.C: Perineurium
options.D: Endoneurium

explanation: The epineurium acts like a sturdy outer jacket holding all the nerve fibers safely together as one big spinal nerve. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T26#GNS211_U3_T26_h2)

question: Where is the nurses' station typically placed in a modern hospital ward?

options.A: At the center to allow clear sightlines
options.B: Near the entrance to restrict visitor access
options.C: At the far end away from patient beds
options.D: Inside the main doctor consulting room

explanation: Central placement helps staff monitor patient activity and respond quickly to call bells or emergencies. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h2)

question: Which group of hormones is made directly from cholesterol?

options.A: Amine hormones
options.B: Steroid hormones
options.C: Peptide hormones
options.D: Protein hormones

explanation: Steroid hormones are built using cholesterol as their base material. Because of this, they share a fat-loving (lipophilic) nature!

question: Why is nursing care for inherited degenerative disorders focused on comfort rather than a cure?

options.A: Medications can completely reverse the genetic mutation if given early.
options.B: Hospital policies restrict long-term curative therapies for chronic illnesses.
options.C: The underlying genetic damage causes progressive and irreversible cell death.
options.D: Clients usually recover spontaneously once they reach middle age.

explanation: Because these conditions involve continuous cellular breakdown from genetics, treatment focuses on managing symptoms and keeping the patient as comfortable as possible.

question: Which gland releases a hormone to raise blood calcium when it drops too low?

options.A: Parathyroid gland
options.B: Thyroid gland
options.C: Adrenal gland
options.D: Pancreas

explanation: Spot on! The tiny parathyroid glands step in with parathyroid hormone to pull calcium back into the blood when levels fall.

question: Which of the following is a good practice, and NOT a common mistake in research proposals?

options.A: Failing to plan proper ethical protections
options.B: Choosing a topic that is far too broad to manage
options.C: Relying heavily on outdated reference materials
options.D: Ensuring alignment between questions and methods

explanation: Making sure your research questions match your methods is a brilliant practice! The other options are classic pitfalls to avoid.

question: Why are modern hospitals moving away from just blaming individuals when mistakes happen?

options.A: Because fixing underlying system flaws prevents future errors better
options.B: Because hospital management no longer cares about errors
options.C: Because nurses refuse to complete incident reports
options.D: Because punishing workers stops all future mistakes

explanation: Looking at system problems instead of just pointing fingers helps fix the root cause so the same mistake doesn't happen again. Great nursing practice starts with understanding this!

question: What does a high PaCO2 level on an arterial blood gas (ABG) report usually tell you?

options.A: Inadequate ventilation or carbon dioxide retention
options.B: Excessive bicarbonate production by the liver
options.C: Too much oxygen being delivered by the ventilator
options.D: Rapid breathing caused by severe emotional anxiety

explanation: If the lungs aren't blowing off air well enough, carbon dioxide builds up in the blood, driving that PaCO2 level right up.

question: What common drink or food substance must a client avoid before having an EEG?

options.A: Caffeine
options.B: Red meat protein
options.C: Complex carbohydrates
options.D: High sodium foods

explanation: Caffeine is a little energy booster that stimulates the nervous system and can mess with normal brain waves during the test. Best to skip the coffee beforehand!

question: What is one of the biggest duties of a community health nurse when dealing with NCDs?

options.A: Manufacturing affordable insulin and blood pressure drugs in local clinics
options.B: Performing major neurosurgeries in rural primary health centers
options.C: Bridging the gap between formal health facilities and grassroots populations
options.D: Enforcing strict national prison sentences for people who eat junk food

explanation: Spot on! Community nurses take health education, screenings, and support right to the doorsteps and neighborhoods where people live.

question: A newly diagnosed patient is terrified and refuses to talk about medication schedules. What is your best first nursing action?

options.A: Report the patient immediately to local public health authorities
options.B: Withhold all educational materials until the patient asks for them
options.C: Force the patient to swallow the first dose of pills right away
options.D: Provide empathetic, non-judgmental support and address emotional distress

explanation: Empathy first! Building trust and helping patients work through their fear and stigma is always the essential first step before teaching them about medications.

question: At what point in pregnancy do the very first structures of the nervous system start to form?

options.A: During the final trimester
options.B: During the third week of pregnancy
options.C: Around the fifth month of gestation
options.D: Immediately after birth

explanation: Spot on! Nervous system development starts super early—during the third week of pregnancy—which is why early antenatal care is so important.

question: What actually happens during the autoimmune destruction of an endocrine gland?

options.A: A genetic mutation stops hormone production entirely
options.B: An infection blocks the blood supply to the organ
options.C: The immune system attacks and destroys glandular cells
options.D: A benign tumor crowds out normal hormone tissue

explanation: Think of it as friendly fire! The immune system gets confused and mistakenly attacks healthy cells in the gland.

question: What is the highest number of skin patches a patient can have to be classified as having paucibacillary leprosy?

options.A: 2 patches
options.B: 20 patches
options.C: 5 patches
options.D: 10 patches

explanation: Paucibacillary simply means 'few bacteria.' Clinically, it's marked by having between one and five skin patches. You're doing great!

question: What is the main goal of system reliability in healthcare?

options.A: How consistently a clinical process produces safe outcomes
options.B: The total number of disciplinary actions taken against staff
options.C: How many patients a single nurse can care for in a shift
options.D: The speed at which doctors answer emergency calls

explanation: You've got this! System reliability simply means how dependably a process delivers safe, correct results every single time.

question: In community health, how would you classify poor sanitation and crowded living conditions?

options.A: The host
options.B: The environment
options.C: The clinical symptom
options.D: The infectious agent
